newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX crude called slightly up tracking ACCESS.

text.p: NYMEX crude was called slightly higher Friday tracking minor gains on ACCESS amid no news, but oil prices were seen vulnerable with spot crude technically weakened after a late session sell-off Thursday.
"The call is basically flat, and I expect us to be pretty much rangebound with not much news, but we could test the $19.80 level which we have been able to hold all week," said a New York dealer.
Crude was called steady to five cents a barrel higher. Heating oil and gasoline were called flat to 0.25 cent a gallon higher.
"If crude breaks $19.80, which is a key level, we could see $19.40 and once again test the lower end of the ($19.00 to $20.00) range," said another New York dealer.
Prompt crude has tested areas between $19.80 and $19.90 three times this week and rebounded.
On Thursday, June crude settled 30 cents a barrel lower at $19.91, breaking out of a bearish wedge formation on the spot continuation chart.
The wedge formation on the spot chart branched off from the April 22 session low and high. The breakout would signify an optimal two-thirds of the move.
But, volume was weak as industry events in Houston had drawn dealers away from the market and were expected to do so again Friday.

Dealers also noted June crude briefly slipped into a three cent contango on the overnight ACCESS session, another bearish signal. Contango means the contract nearer in time is less expensive than the later contract and usually reflects ample prompt supply.
June heating oil ended 0.59 cent a gallon lower Thursday at 54.33 cents while June gasoline settled 0.22 cent a gallon higher at 62.63 cents.
"If we are going to get any strength today, it will be from gasoline," said a trader, noting gasoline demand has entered into its seasonally strongest periods of spring and summer.
-- Harry Milling, New York Energy Desk, 212-859-1761
